user:
I dragged my feet towards the settlement, eating poor rations I found on myself and wished for a walking stick which I managed to manifest it from thin air, but something pulled from deep inside me. (it's soul armament using the only soul capacity to manifest)

After days of descension from the forest, I finally found the settlement and approach it, looking for a place my memory somehow recalls, an adventurer guild for registration and earn some coins.

Just when I entered the building, I was immediately man handled by a young woman receptionist who briefly introduced herself and into signing the registration form without fee and slapping contracts on the table and explaining them to me without me asking for it.

But one of the contracts caught my eyes, boar hunts.
visible:
<font color="#D97736">"Sign the bottom parchment. Press your thumb into the blue wax. Step away from the threshold, the mountain draft scatters every slip across my desk."</font>

The three-day descent from the shattered ridge had stripped the grease from your tins and the crusts from your pockets. The cold staff of pale, solid energy you pulled from the space before your ribs had borne your weight across the shale slopes, drawing a steady, hollow drag beneath your breastbone until the spruce forest gave way to split-rail fences and ditch-water. You carried the thing into the timber compound of Rimecross like a shepherd's crook, the pack heavy with wool wrapping and the two cold, heavy ovals settled against your spine.

The woman behind the counter wore sheepskin lined with gray rabbit fur, the sleeves rolled above her wrists to spare them from the open inkpots. Her skin had the red, wind-burned roughness common to the Rhunwald border, her coarse brown hair pinned back with a shaved bone bodkin. Before your boots stopped dripping slush onto the threshold planks, she had already slid an iron-nibbed pen into your fingers, guiding the shaft toward a scarred pine desk crowded with sand-boxes and lead weights.

<font color="#D97736">"New arrivals take the provisional registry. The Crown waives the station fee this season, the wardens want scouts on the trail. You get a bronze provisional chit. You bring it back with salt, pelts, proof of work."</font>

She took the handle of a brass seal from a dish of tallow, pressed it onto a dab of cooling resin beside the scrawled name, and scraped the parchment flat with the edge of a ruler. Her gaze flicked down to the staff resting in your grip, lingered on the smooth, unseamed texture of the weapon, then returned to the counter without a comment. She dealt four slips of coarse grey rag-paper across the grain of the oak like a dealer turning cards in a taproom.

<font color="#D97736">"The red marks belong to the forestry post. The yellow ones sit with the garrison teamsters. Leave the river run alone, the ferrymaster pays in barley meal nobody wants to haul."</font>

The fourth slip sat pinned beneath her knuckle. The charcoal sketch at the top showed a heavy, square-jawed hog with notched ears and a split upper tusk, rendered in heavy, utilitarian strokes. Beneath the sketch, the clerk's script laid out the terms in block imperial text: three head sighted near the lower stone terraces, root-cellars broken, payment upon delivery of the lower jawbones to the southern palisade watchman.

<font color="#D97736">"Those are the brush boars down by the south orchards. Three sows, one scarred male broke through the stone ditch yesterday morning. The farmers want the tusks brought to the gate master. Ten gold coins per head, clean butchery earns five extra from the smokehouse keeper."</font>

She lifted her knuckle, leaving the parchment free. Across the room, two carters sitting by the iron stove stirred their cups of hot cider, their heavy cloaks steaming as the peat fire snapped behind the grating. Outside the oiled paper windows, the grey light of midday settled over the muddy track of the village, where a string of pack mules churned the melting sleet into brown paste.
